context:
Goal: the rule file says the same as your ruling on which model the design reviewer runs.
Problem (rule): CLAUDE.md lines 22-23 (rule roles-sonnet-is-the-ceiling) still list the design reviewer among the agents that run Opus. Your ruling own-756 (14:01 CST Nov 13, item 756) moved the design reviewer to Sonnet high. Whether your ruling covers the rule text, or the edit needs its own grant, is your call: your grant covers only the act it names.
Based on (read): the coordinator's note 16:40 CST Nov 13, from lane model-layout-to-table (PR #3286); ruling own-756-design-reviewer-sonnet on the roadmap branch. Triage has not read the two lines.
Departs from: main — CLAUDE.md says Opus for the design reviewer; this changes it to Sonnet high, in the same PR as the model table.
Meanwhile: the lane leaves the rule text alone and builds the table.
home: ruling own-756-design-reviewer-sonnet; step model-layout-to-table; PR #3286; CLAUDE.md lines 22-23

options.gain: The rule file matches your ruling and the table.
options.label: Yes: edit CLAUDE.md lines 22-23 to say the design reviewer runs Sonnet high, with the model table (Recommended)
options.lose: One rule-file edit goes in the lane's PR for your yes.

options.label: Not yet: leave the rule text
options.lose: The rule says Opus while the table says Sonnet, and a session may follow the rule.

reply: Filed as ruling own-776-a-design-reviewer-lines and sent to the lane. Your question, why this sits in CLAUDE.md: that rule file lists which model each agent role runs, and every session loads it, so sessions follow it when they spawn. You are right that the spawn could carry it instead; I filed a follow-up step so the rule points at the model table rather than repeating model names.
short: Edit the rule text on the design reviewer's model?
title: Edit CLAUDE.md so the design reviewer runs Sonnet high, as you ruled?
why: The rule file still says Opus; a rule-file edit needs your word.
